title: Democracy and Security Network
gist: Program page for GMF's Democracy and Security Network, which argues that norms against using militaries for domestic political ends are crumbling worldwide, with leaders promoting officers on party loyalty; it flags the US, Poland, Turkey, and Hungary and is focusing research on US domestic deployments and military involvement in elections.

themes.theme: Erosion of norms against domestic political use of militaries

insights.claim: GMF's Democracy and Security Network asserts that norms against using the military to satisfy domestic political priorities are crumbling worldwide.
insights.speaker: German Marshall Fund
insights.so_what: A global weakening of civil-military guardrails raises tail risks of domestic instability and institutional erosion that markets typically underprice in developed democracies.
insights.quote: Norms against using the military to satisfy domestic political priorities are crumbling worldwide

insights.claim: Political leaders are increasingly selecting general officers and other military leaders based on perceived party loyalty rather than merit or ability to offer independent military advice.
insights.speaker: German Marshall Fund
insights.so_what: Loyalty-based promotion degrades the quality of independent military advice, increasing the risk of strategic miscalculation and readiness shortfalls.
insights.quote: political leaders are increasingly relying on general officers and other military leaders based on their perceived party loyalty rather than on merit

insights.claim: GMF argues the politicization of the US military has serious implications for the health and quality of American democracy.
insights.speaker: German Marshall Fund
insights.so_what: Frames US civil-military relations as a live governance risk factor, relevant to assessments of US institutional stability and country risk.

themes.theme: Comparative cases of military politicization in Europe and Turkey

insights.claim: Poland, Turkey, and Hungary are cited as countries where leaders have politicized the military and undermined readiness, public trust, and accountability.
insights.speaker: German Marshall Fund
insights.so_what: Politicized militaries in NATO members on the alliance's eastern and southern flanks can weaken collective defense credibility at a time of elevated European security risk.
insights.quote: other countries such as Poland, Turkey, and Hungary have also seen leaders politicize the military and undermine readiness, public trust, and accountability

themes.theme: US domestic military deployments and elections as a focus area

insights.claim: GMF's recent research agenda centers on the risk of the US military being used around elections and in domestic deployments, with pieces titled 'Military Meddling at the Polls', 'Tracking Domestic Deployments of the U.S. Military', and 'The Military and Elections, Part II: Deploy First, Litigate Later'.
insights.speaker: German Marshall Fund
insights.so_what: Signals that analysts see a non-trivial risk of military involvement in the US electoral process, a potential source of political and market volatility around elections.

insights.claim: The network's strategy to prevent or mitigate military politicization in countries at risk of democratic backsliding is to collaborate with three communities: retired military, legal professionals, and public opinion leaders.
insights.speaker: German Marshall Fund
insights.so_what: Identifies the institutional counterweights (veterans, courts/lawyers, opinion leaders) whose mobilization would signal escalation in civil-military tensions.
insights.quote: collaborating with three critical communities: retired military, legal professionals, and public opinion leaders
